source.title: Grokking vs. Learning: Same Features, Different Encodings
source.authors: Dmitry Manning-Coe; Jacopo Gliozzi; A. G. Stapleton; Edward Hirst; Giuseppe De Tomasi; B. Bradlyn; David S. Berman

record.tranche_reason: The study trains modular-addition models and measures training/test behavior and learned features, using a setup that conceptually tests grokking and its development. It also tests the phenomenon in an Ising classification task.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training curves, feature measurements, and pruning/compressibility results. It also discusses prior grokking results, but those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own modular-addition MLPs and Ising CNNs. It switches between grokking and steady learning with the initialization weight multiplier. It reports training curves, feature (Fourier IPR, energy-correlation) measurements and their development through the plateau. These bear on V1 (delayed generalization), V2 (progress measures during the plateau), V3 (initialization scale switching delay on image-like data) and V6 (same features across regimes). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Grokked and steadily learned models learn the same features (Fourier modes; Ising energy) but can encode them with different efficiency. A 'compressive regime' of steady learning, absent in grokking, gives up to 25x compression. Plateau development is task-dependent: progress measures exist for modular addition but not for Ising. Peak compressibility comes just after the plateau, and grokking follows a near-straight path in FIM model space.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition with P=113, a one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP, 70% of examples for training, and initialization weight scaling to induce grokking; also adds an Ising CNN classification task.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking versus steady learning changes with initialization weight multiplier. The modular-addition compressive regime depends on other parameters and disappears when batch size is increased from 64 to 200; the high-compression result uses weight decay 3 × 10−4.

fits_no_version.finding: Steadily learned modular-addition models in a 'compressive regime' are more prunable than grokked ones. There is a linear trade-off between compressibility and train loss, absent in grokking and in Ising, and it disappears at batch size 200. At weight decay 3e-4, steady learning reaches 25x compression. Fisher pruning shows grokked models are not necessarily more compressible.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokked models are not more compressible than steadily learned models with the same features; compressibility tracks init scale and other hyperparameters, not grokking.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The study uses toy tasks and does not test training-set-size dependence. Some training and pruning values are presented graphically; several comparisons are averaged over seeds without numerical uncertainty estimates. Feature-development results differ by task, and the compressive regime is parameter-dependent.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (train fraction fixed at 70%).
Removal of memorizing components; whether the progress measure quantitatively predicts jump timing.
Text and molecule data; weight norm as a separate intervention; explicit lazy-to-rich characterization.
Entire version: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Entire version: no memorization-vs-generalization circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, or ungrokking test. The compressibility results measure a different construct.
Entire version: optimizer and floating-point choices are not controlled (Adam only).

missing.what: FIM cosine similarity to the origin direction: the Ising grokking trajectory is near 1 (weight-decay dominated, straight path), while modular addition is much lower (features develop before the transition).
Fourier IPR breakdown in compressive and high-weight-decay regimes (IPR falls about tenfold), showing the learned representation depends on hyperparameters.

FIM step-magnitude bump marking the grokking start and end (roots at epochs ~19-20 and ~46-47 for modular addition; 2200-2400 and 6200-6400 for Ising). This gives the length of the modular-addition grokking period.

record.verdict_notes: The compressibility rows were wrongly linked to V5 with a 'challenges' label. V5 concerns weight-decay-driven preference for an efficient generalizing circuit over memorization, critical dataset size and ungrokking, none of which is measured here. Grokking is induced via init scale (Omnigrok method), which is legitimate for V3 but makes the V1 evidence an induced-regime case with short delays. Text inconsistencies: Section 5 cites Appendix F for the batch-size result, but it is in Appendix D. Seed counts differ between the main text (Ising 5, mod-add 10) and the appendix captions (Ising 10, mod-add 5).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size to test whether smaller sets require more optimization.
It measures feature-development proxies, not removal of memorizing components directly; it does not establish that those measures predict the accuracy jump in advance.
It tests Ising image classification and initialization weight scale, but not text, molecules, or weight norm as a separate intervention.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The study measures pruning-based compressibility, but does not establish that low norm causes a more efficient generalizing circuit, nor test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.

The study compares learned features across training regimes in the same task architectures; it does not systematically vary architecture or establish convergence to an identical algorithm across such variations.
No controlled test of adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax limits is reported.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Training and test accuracy tracked during training

conditions.value: weight multiplier sweep; grokking begins at approximately w0=0.4
curves averaged over ten random initialization seeds

rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over epochs
rows.value: figure only; the paper defines grokking as test accuracy reaching its near-maximum later than training accuracy, and reports the transition at approximately w0=0.4
rows.uncertainty: Curves averaged over ten seeds; uncertainty values not stated
rows.note: The reported setup and curves show delayed generalization in modular addition. Training-set-size dependence is not tested.
rows.check: Value is figure-only. Grokking is induced by a large initialization multiplier, so R1 also bears on V3's init-scale switching. The modular-addition grok times are short (tens to a few hundred epochs), so 'long after' is only weakly shown.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked mean hidden-neuron Fourier inverse participation ratio during training
rows.measure: Fourier-basis localization measured by mean IPR
rows.value: The model improves its localization in the Fourier basis throughout the plateau, while accuracy and loss do not improve
rows.note: This is a continuous feature-development measure; it is not a direct measurement of removal of memorizing components.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.1, paragraph discussing Fourier localization during the plateau; Figure 6.

rows.subject: Ising CNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked feature correlations across layers during training
rows.measure: Layer-wise representation of energy, magnetization, and absolute magnetization
rows.value: All three metrics are roughly constant across layers during the plateau; the paper reports no sign of model development before generalization
rows.note: The authors characterize development during the plateau as task-dependent.

rows.subject: Ising CNN
rows.operation_detail: Varied initialization weight multiplier to move between grokking and steady learning
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy/loss over training
rows.value: The regimes interpolate smoothly with initialization scale; grokking sets in at approximately w0=3
rows.uncertainty: Curves averaged over five seeds; uncertainty values not stated
rows.note: The Ising task is the paper's non-algorithmic image-classification setting.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Magnitude-pruned trained models and compared compressibility across initialization multipliers
rows.measure: Compressibility from area under pruning-accuracy curve; relation to end-model training loss
rows.value: Compressibility improves systematically as the weight multiplier is reduced; a linear trade-off with end training loss emerges in this regime
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over seeds; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The paper calls this a parameter-dependent compressive regime of steady learning.
rows.check: Compares terminal compressibility of steadily learned vs grokked models across init scales. V5 predicts neither this nor a critical dataset size or ungrokking, so it should not be linked to V5. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Magnitude-pruned trained models and compared compressibility across initialization multipliers
rows.measure: Compressibility as a function of initialization multiplier
rows.value: The paper reports no significant dependence of compressibility on w0 in the grokking regime
rows.note: The grokking curves are described as overlapping; this does not support a general claim that grokked models are more compressible.
rows.check: No w0 dependence of compressibility in the grokking regime. This is not a V5 measure (no memorization-vs-generalization efficiency, no dataset-size threshold).

rows.subject: Ising CNN
rows.operation_detail: Magnitude-pruned trained models and compared compressibility across initialization multipliers
rows.value: No clear relationship between compressibility and weight multiplier, and no meaningful trade-off between compressibility and end loss
rows.note: The study reports no analogous compressive phase for this task.
rows.check: Ising compressibility vs weight multiplier is not a V5 measure.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Magnitude-pruned models in a higher-weight-decay parameter regime
rows.measure: Accuracy retained after pruning and resulting compressibility
rows.value: 95% of weights can be cut for a 5% drop in accuracy; compressibility is 25x that of the base model and 5x the compression achieved at the lower weight multiplier
rows.note: The paper also reports that a 30% larger weight decay no longer lets models learn; the exceptionally compressed regime is close to breakdown.
rows.check: High-weight-decay compression in steady learning (w0=1) is about pruning of the final model, not the weight-decay efficiency account of grokking.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared magnitude-pruning compressibility after changing batch size
rows.value: Increasing batch size to 200 eliminates the compressive regime; there is no significant increase in compressibility at lower weight multiplier
rows.note: This result shows that the compression effect depends on training parameters.
rows.check: The batch-size control on the compressive regime concerns the same non-V5 construct. The main text says Appendix F, but the result is in Appendix D / Fig 14.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured terminal hidden-neuron Fourier localization with mean IPR
rows.measure: Mean Fourier-basis IPR across hidden neurons
rows.uncertainty: Comparable mean IPR reported for the steady-learning regime; no error bar stated
rows.note: The authors interpret the localization as neurons predominantly processing sine and cosine components of a single frequency.

rows.subject: modular addition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured terminal hidden-neuron Fourier localization with mean IPR
rows.measure: Mean Fourier-basis IPR across hidden neurons
rows.uncertainty: Comparable mean IPR reported for the grokking regime; no error bar stated
rows.note: The authors conclude that grokked and steadily learned models learn the same task features.

rows.subject: Ising CNN
rows.operation_detail: Correlated final-layer neuron pre-activations with physical features of the input
rows.measure: Correlation of final-layer neuron pre-activations with energy
rows.value: Every final-layer neuron is described as perfectly correlated or anti-correlated with the energy
rows.note: The authors identify energy as the dominant learned feature.

rows.subject: Ising CNN
rows.operation_detail: Correlated final-layer neuron pre-activations with physical features of the input
rows.measure: Correlation of final-layer neuron pre-activations with energy
rows.value: Energy is the dominant feature overall, but three seeds show significant deviation from perfect energy correlation and instead correlate with raw magnetization
rows.uncertainty: The paper describes seed variation; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The authors report noisier feature representations in the grokking regime than in steady learning.
rows.check: The Fig 13 caption says the dominant behaviour is to 'learn the magnetization', which conflicts with the text naming energy as dominant. State is kept as partial, on the text's three deviating seeds.

relationships.condition: Modular addition P=113, 70% train fraction, Adam, large init multiplier (w0>~0.4)
relationships.reason: Test accuracy saturates after train accuracy by the paper's 5%-threshold definition (R1, figure-only). The delay is short and induced by init scale.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy saturated shortly after training accuracy under the study's 5% threshold definition, with the delay induced by initialization scale.
